sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2-Codex
sources.evidence: Dated December 18, 2025; releases this GPT-5.2 coding variant across Codex surfaces for paid ChatGPT users that day, with API access forthcoming. Describes vision, tool use and context compaction.

sources.title: GPT-5.2-Codex model reference
sources.evidence: Exact model reference: GPT-5.2 variant; text and image input, text output; 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens; low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning; Responses, function calling and prompt caching. The undated default identifier is gpt-5.2-codex; current status is Shut down.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: January 14, 2026 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.2-codex to Responses. February 3 says the faster inference stack did not change the model or its weights.

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex
sources.evidence: December 18, 2025 original card, retrieved as a complete PDF. Describes this exact coding variant, compaction and RL training with simulated conflicting user edits in section 4.2.2. Does not disclose total or active parameters or a complete production network architecture.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Explains cached key/value projections in Transformer attention layers and includes an exact gpt-5.2-codex Responses compaction example. With exact-model prompt-caching support, supports only a broad Transformer inference, not a full block inventory or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses PDF processing extracts text and page images for vision-capable models. Combined with this exact model reference’s vision and Responses support, establishes PDF as a supported API input format.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 deprecation section explicitly lists gpt-5.2-codex with a July 23, 2026 shutdown date.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex
sources.evidence: February 5, 2026 announcement includes an exact GPT-5.2-Codex (xhigh) appendix comparison column. Its entries are benchmark scores, not total or active parameter counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.3-Codex System Card
sources.evidence: Later card retrieved as a complete PDF; includes exact GPT-5.2-Codex safety and capability comparisons, including CTF and CVEBench. These disclose evaluation results, not GPT-5.2-Codex parameter counts or a complete network architecture. Later sibling training claims are not transferred.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current service terms grant limited service-use rights and reserve OpenAI intellectual property; used only to support a descriptive proprietary classification, not to reconstruct the terms in force at launch.

sources.title: OpenAI model catalog
sources.evidence: Lists GPT-5.2-Codex among hosted/retired models and separately identifies the gpt-oss open-weight models; no weight distribution or open-weight license is supplied for GPT-5.2-Codex.

name.note: Use the exact official hyphenated product name.

developer.note: OpenAI published the model announcement and original system card.

family.note: The exact model is expressly a GPT-5.2 version optimized for coding; family classification follows the base generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public Codex release was December 18, 2025, not the December 11 release of general GPT-5.2. Responses API availability followed January 14, 2026.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted Codex and subsequently the API. The reviewed first-party release, model reference and catalog provide no downloadable weights and distinguish gpt-oss as open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted OpenAI model; no named open-weight license is disclosed. Current service terms support this classification but do not establish historical launch contract wording.

parameters_b.note: Not disclosed in the reviewed exact model reference, original system card and its exact-model training section, or later GPT-5.3-Codex announcement/card comparisons. Searched first-party exact-model training and interpretability leads; no usable count found. No value inferred from branding, sibling models, benchmark scores or the February inference speedup. This is a bounded primary-source review.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact-model active parameter count or routing breakdown found in the reviewed original and later primary material. Do not substitute a sibling count or equate total and active parameters.

architecture.note: Qualified operational inference: the exact model reference explicitly supports prompt caching; the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 Prompt Caching 201 guide explains Transformer attention key/value reuse and includes an exact gpt-5.2-codex example. This supports a broad Transformer classification only. Original/later cards and first-party training/interpretability leads did not disclose the complete production block inventory, dense versus MoE structure, layer/head counts or numerical size.

context_window.note: Last-documented context window is 400,000 tokens; exact reference also specifies 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. Compaction permits cumulative work across requests and does not enlarge the per-request context. Documentation is historical capability evidence, not proof of an operating endpoint.

modalities.note: Native documented model modalities are text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API input format: the file-input guide processes PDF text and page images for vision models via Responses, both explicitly supported by this exact model. No native audio/video input or image/audio output is asserted.

reasoning.note: Exact reference lists reasoning token support and low, medium, high and xhigh effort settings; no none setting is borrowed from general GPT-5.2.

tool_call.note: The exact model reference explicitly lists function_calling as a feature and supported Responses tool.

description.value: GPT-5.2 coding variant with reasoning, text and image input, function calling and context compaction.
description.note: Plain description restricted to exact-model documented capabilities; avoids unsupported ranking and network-size claims.

patch.name: GPT-5.2-Codex
patch.description: GPT-5.2 coding variant with reasoning, text and image input, function calling and context compaction.

sources.label: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex

patch.notes: Released in Codex on 2025-12-18; Responses API release was 2026-01-14. The undated gpt-5.2-codex identifier is not an immutable dated checkpoint; the reviewed reference gives no separately dated target or complete alias history. Last-documented limits are 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens. Compaction does not enlarge that context window. PDF is an API input format processed into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified inference from exact-model prompt-caching support and the applicable first-party caching mechanism; dense/MoE structure, full block inventory, total parameters and active parameters remain undisclosed in the reviewed sources. The API was deprecated on 2026-04-22 and shut down on 2026-07-23; the current model reference says Shut down. No live endpoint request was made, and this API retirement date is not asserted as a separate Codex product retirement date.

summary: Corrected the name, family and earliest public release date to GPT-5.2-Codex, gpt-5.2 and 2025-12-18; added proprietary classification, qualified Transformer inference and a factual description. Confirmed reasoning, function calling, text/image input, PDF API input, text output and 400,000-token context with explicit input/output limits. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after original and later exact-model primary-source review. Recorded the later API release, undated identifier, compaction distinction and July 23, 2026 API shutdown.
